summary: The 1912 Classical Revival powerhouse on 20th Street between Buildings 101 and 104, designed by Charles Peter Weeks, which generated compressed air and distributed electricity for the shipyard and still housed BAE Systems' electrical service when rehabilitation began. Orton rebuilt it as office space with a mezzanine and a rear addition (about 15,300-18,000 sq ft) and subleased it to JUUL Labs for ten years; the current occupant is unknown.

milestones.text: Built as the Union Iron Works powerhouse to Charles Peter Weeks's design; equipment dating from 1913-1914 remained in 2013
Port Commission endorses the Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan (Resolution 10-27), which calls for a National Register district and rehabilitation of the 20th Street buildings

Port Commission awards the 20th Street Historic Buildings opportunity to Orton Development after a 2011 RFP; Exclusive Negotiating Agreement approved April 2012; term sheet endorsed October 2012 (Board of Supervisors December 2012)

Historic Preservation Commission informational hearing on the rehabilitation of the ten 20th Street Historic Buildings (case 2013.1168E): ~270,000 gsf existing plus ~69,000 gsf of new mezzanines, ~334,000 gsf total
Union Iron Works Historic District listed in the National Register of Historic Places (NRIS 14000150), giving the project access to federal historic tax credits
Port Commission Resolution 14-33 approves the Lease Disposition and Development Agreement and 66-year Master Lease (L-15814) with Historic Pier 70, LLC (Orton) and adopts CEQA findings
Master lease approved by the Board of Supervisors and fully executed, giving Orton site control; construction commences thereafter (September 2015 per the National Trust)
Permanent financing for the Historic Core project achieved

Port Commission update: six of eight buildings complete, Buildings 101 and 102 still under construction, project 100% subleased except two atrium retail spaces; total cost revised from $81.9M to an estimated $127.0M
Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation receives a Governor's Historic Preservation Award
2013 plan: ODI to redevelop the 11,266 sq ft former Compressor House as a restaurant with an exterior dining deck, after the Port removes BAE's electrical facilities

Building abated of PCB electrical equipment; new shipyard electrical service occupies part of the basement; rehabilitation of the remainder under way with completion anticipated in 2019; public disappointment noted that it will be office, not a restaurant
Port commissioners discuss shortening or ending JUUL Labs' ten-year sublease of Building 102 (and 104); no action taken
Rehabilitation and tenant improvements scheduled for completion (Port's 2019 milestone list)
Rehabilitation profiled: seismic bracing, mezzanine, 2,600 sq ft rear addition with rooftop deck, one of four historic compressors retained; Marcy Wong Donn Logan wins a Metamorphosis Award for it

costs.what: Estimated hard cost of the Building 102 rehabilitation (future expenditure estimate in 2018; $3.1M at 2014 approvals)

facts.value: Orton Development, Inc. through Historic Pier 70, LLC (66-year master lease L-15814 from the Port of San Francisco)
Marcy Wong Donn Logan Architects (design architect); Mark Hulbert, Preservation Architecture (historic architect)

Developer equity up to $14 million plus loans; Port participation rent of 50% of revenues above debt and a 14% equity return; sources in 2018: Port capital $1.8M, Seismic Safety Loan $23.6M, historic tax credit equity $20.4M, private debt and equity $81.2M
Contributing resource to the Union Iron Works Historic District (NRHP, listed April 17, 2014)
Tall rectangular concrete building with hipped mission-tile roof, five arched bays, terra cotta shell frieze and copper cornice
128 ft 6 in by 42 ft 4 in by 48 ft tall
8,428 (NRHP, first floor and basement); 11,266 before and 15,331 after rehabilitation (Port 2019 Table 1); 15,500 original and just over 18,000 after per Retrofit magazine
Office (subleased to JUUL Labs, 10-year term, entire building less the Port's basement electrical room)
JUUL Labs subleased Building 102 (and 104); the presence of an e-cigarette maker on Port land drew public objection in 2018-2019
Powerhouse No. 1 Electric: offices, four air compressors, three rotary converters, switchboard and transformers on the main floor; still serving some of BAE Systems' electrical needs in 2013
'Building 102 key historic features' listed by the Port as publicly accessible

open_questions: Current tenant: JUUL's sublease was to run ten years from completion (2019), but no source after 2020 confirms JUUL is still in Building 102 or names a successor.
Completion / certificate of occupancy date: the Port anticipated 2019; the November 2020 profile describes the finished building without a date.
The square-footage figures disagree by source (8,428 NRHP floor area vs 11,266 Port pre-rehab vs 15,500 magazine); the NRHP figure may exclude the basement.
